newsitem.title: UK: EU denies other states' pension woes could hit UK.
newsitem.headline: EU denies other states' pension woes could hit UK.

text.p: The European Commission on Thursday denied claims by a committee of Britain's parliament that British taxpayers could suffer under monetary union because of huge pension fund liabilities in other EU states.
"This is not the case," it said in a statement.

Earlier, a report by parliament's Social Services Committee said the unfunded liabilities in countries such as France and Germany could either fuel inflation in a Europe which had adopted a single currency or push up interest rates.
In either event, it said, Britons, most of whose pensions are fully funded, would suffer.
"There will be no common fiscal policy, so the UK could not be called upon, under a single currency, to pay for the possible profligacy of any other country," the Commission statement said.
"Nor is there any possibility of this issue having an effect on interest rates."
The statement said any EU country borrowing heavily to fund its pension liabilities could, under the rules of Stage Three of Economic and Monetary Union, face heavy fines.
